name: Portuguese Mozambique
alt: Captaincy-General of Mozambique, Sofala and Rivers of Sena

successors.name: Mozambique (People's Republic of Mozambique, then Republic of Mozambique)
successors.text: 'Covering a total area of 801,590 km2' in the early 1970s

ledger.x: 1505: the Portuguese found their East African colony at Sofala.

1507: the Portuguese take the Island of Mozambique, whose Cidade de Pedra is the capital from 1507 ('gained control of the Island of Mozambique and the port city of Sofala in the early 16th century').
1530s: Sena and Tete become Portuguese garrison towns on the Zambezi.
1545: Lourenço Marques founds a settlement on Maputo Bay.
1629: the Mwenemutapa becomes a Portuguese vassal after Masapa.
1629: Portugal recovers the Tete country.
1632: 'a Portuguese captain led an army to subdue the Valley from Quelimane to Sena, and conquered Manyika.'
1678: Mukombwe 'refused to acknowledge their suzerainty in 1678', ending the Mutapa vassalage.
1727: the Portuguese found a trading post at Inhambane ('In 1727, they founded a trading post at Inhambane').
1752: Mozambique gets its own Captaincy-General of Mozambique, Sofala and the Rivers of Sena, 'independent from that of the Portuguese State of India' (listed 1752-1836).
1781: the Portuguese 'permanently occupied Delagoa Bay' (Lourenço Marques).
1882: the Gaza kingdom becomes a Portuguese protectorate (infobox: 'Independent Kingdom (1824-1882), Portuguese protectorate (1882-1895)').
1885: Portugal annexes Chidima.

1891: the colony becomes the State of Eastern Africa ('1891-1893: State of Eastern Africa (Estado da África Oriental)'); the Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 11 June 1891 sets its western boundaries and Manicaland passes to Britain.
1891 (bridge): Nampula province, the mainland behind the Island of Mozambique, is drawn Portuguese from the State of Eastern Africa ('1891-1893: State of Eastern Africa').
11 June 1891: the Anglo-Portuguese Treaty, 'signed in Lisbon on 11 June 1891', 'fixed the boundaries' and gave Portugal 'more territory in the Zambezi valley' than the unratified 1890 treaty.
March 1893: the Niassa Company is chartered 'from the Ruvuma River to the Lúrio River', 'more than 160,000 square km' (Cabo Delgado and Niassa).
28 December 1895: the Gaza protectorate ends with the capture of Gungunhana at Chaimite.
28 December 1895: Portugal annexes the Gaza lands.
1897: Chioko's resistance attacks Portuguese centres in the Zambezi valley.
1902: the rising ends.
28 June 1919: Mozambique receives the Kionga Triangle.
1951: 'it became an overseas province'.
25 June 1975: Mozambique becomes independent.
ledger.cpn: Mozambique (People's Republic of Mozambique, then Republic of Mozambique)

wars.name: Mutapa-Portuguese war of 1629-1632
wars.outcome: 1629 Masapa and the terms of vassalage; 1631 the Mavhura-Portuguese army is routed by Kapararidze; 1632 a Portuguese captain subdues the Valley from Quelimane to Sena and conquers Manyika.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Gaza Empire
wars.outcome: The Gaza Empire was 'annexed in 1895' after the Battle of Magul; Gungunhana was captured at Chaimite on 28 December 1895 and exiled to the Azores.

wars.name: Pacification of the Zambezi valley and the Chioko rising
wars.outcome: 'the pacification of the Zambezi valley followed, between 1895 and 1902, culminating in the Barue campaign'; Chioko's coalition held most of Tete province by 1901 and was suppressed in 1902.

certainty.note: Coastal forts, river posts and prazos; no frontier is described on the pages opened.

The Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 11 June 1891 fixed the boundaries with Nyasaland and the BSAC territories; the Rovuma boundary and the occupation of the north (Niassa Company, to 1929) are not dated on the pages opened.
